sections.h2: What is the quickest way to sell a house in Troy?
sections.html:
Troy owners can price a listing to draw several bids, sell privately to someone they know, or accept an as-is purchase for cash. Troy's median home value tops Sterling Heights, Taylor and Walker in the Census figures, so weeks of preparation can pay off, while a cash deal suits an owner with no time to spare.

Owners' median home value is $420,300 and median household income is $120,045 for 2020 through 2024. At that level, a buyer's inspection report carries weight. A house needing major work, an estate, or a job transfer can push a seller toward one offer from a buyer who handles the repairs.

  • Agent listing: suits a house in good order and an owner who can absorb inspections and lender timelines.
  • Private sale: realistic only if you can produce a contract and a deed the Oakland County Register of Deeds will take.
  • Cash offer: fits when speed, privacy or the state of the house outweigh a top price.

sections.h2: Where is Troy, and how did the city develop?
sections.html:
Troy covers 33.45 square miles of land in Oakland County and was estimated at 88,733 people in mid-2025. Sterling Heights lies along its eastern border.

Buyers bought the first recorded land in 1819, and Troy Corners grew where a settler purchased 160 acres in today's north-central Troy. A township formed in 1827, and pieces of it later went to Birmingham, Clawson and Royal Oak. The rest became the city in 1955, partly to keep neighbors from taking more territory. Growth was sharp: 19,402 people in 1960, 39,419 in 1970, and 87,294 at the 2020 Census.

The climate table for the 48098 ZIP code shows a January average low of 22 degrees Fahrenheit and about 32 inches of precipitation a year, which is why roofs and gutters get attention in inspections.

sections.h2: How do Troy's income and housing numbers compare?
sections.html:
Income, schooling and home values all run high here. Almost two-thirds of adults aged 25 and over hold a bachelor's degree, and nearly one resident in three was born abroad.

sections.h2: How large is Troy's commercial base?
sections.html:
Troy's economy reaches well past its resident count. The Census Bureau reports retail sales of $4.17 billion for 2022, which works out to $47,709 per resident, the highest per-person figure of the four cities in this comparison. Health care and social assistance brought in $2.28 billion, and accommodation and food service sales reached $536 million.

The same release shows 65.8% of people 16 and older in the civilian labor force and 2,577 veterans living in the city. For a seller, the commercial strength means steady demand from people who work at the office towers and medical campuses and want a short drive home.

City Hall at 500 W. Big Beaver Road houses the Assessor, the Clerk and the Treasurer, so records requests and tax receipts can usually be handled in one trip. Dog licenses come through Oakland County Animal Control, and Troy does not impose a general business license.

sections.h2: Which employers, malls and schools shape Troy demand?
sections.html:
Big Beaver Road anchors the business district. Automotive and financial offices line it, the Somerset Collection mall (180 stores and a skywalk) and the Oakland Mall draw shoppers, and the Top of Troy houses a PNC office. Walsh College and several branch campuses operate in town, and the Troy Historic Village preserves ten buildings from the city's past.

Seven school districts reach into the city. Troy School District serves most addresses with twelve elementary schools, four middle schools and two zoned high schools, Troy High and Athens High, and it hosts the International Academy's eastern campus. Avondale, Birmingham and Warren Consolidated each operate an elementary school inside Troy. Bloomfield Hills, Royal Oak and Lamphere hold smaller pieces.

With that patchwork, neighbors can belong to different districts. Name the district in your listing, and verify it with the assessor first if the address sits near a boundary.

sections.h2: How do assessments and tax bills affect a Troy seller?
sections.html:
The assessor values property at 50% of market value under the state constitution and administers Principal Residence Exemption claims and Property Transfer Affidavits. For 2026 the office projects combined State Equalized Value above $10 billion.

  • Summer: mailed July 1, payable until September 1. Afterward a 4% penalty applies, then half a percent monthly from October 1.
  • Winter: mailed December 1, payable until February 14, then a 3% penalty.
  • Current-year balances move to the Oakland County Treasurer on March 1 (248.858.0611, option 7).

Troy collects for seven school districts plus the county, Oakland Schools, Macomb Intermediate and several county authorities. School levies differ by district and by whether a home is a principal residence, so similar houses can receive unlike bills. Homeowners who are 62 or older, disabled or veterans, with income of $40,000 or below, may defer to April 30 by applying through September 15.

Under Michigan law the buyer's taxable value uncaps the year after a transfer. Prorations are set by contract, and the Treasurer's Office at 248.524.3333 can describe the amount due on a given date.

sections.h2: What does selling in Oakland County cost at the Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
Transfer tax is the seller's, due within 15 days of delivery of the deed (MCL 207.523). The state share is $3.75 per $500 (MCL 207.525). MCL 207.504 sets the county share at 55 cents per $500 where a county has fewer than 2,000,000 residents, so confirm the Oakland County figure with the register before closing.

The Register of Deeds answers at 248-858-0597 or deeds@oaklandcountymi.gov, on weekdays, with counter hours starting at 8:30 in the morning. It files deeds, mortgages and foreclosure records, and its Super Index lets you pull recorded documents back to January 1, 1964.

Gifts to children and grandchildren, deeds in foreclosure and court orders with no stated price are exempt under MCL 207.526, and the deed must name the exemption on its face.

sections.h2: What Troy property rules should be settled before showings?
sections.html:
Code Enforcement publishes the complaints it handles most often. A quick walk around the lot can head off a notice during your listing.

  • Lawn grass and weeds stay under 8 inches between May 1 and October 31, including the strip to the road.
  • Snow over 2 inches and ice come off public sidewalks within 24 hours after a storm.
  • Cars parked on private land must be licensed and running, and RVs cannot sit on the street.
  • Temporary signs are allowed on private property, while signs in the public right-of-way are removed.
  • Bins go to the curb after 5 p.m. the day before pickup, and branches near sidewalks need trimming to 8 feet.

Keep open house and yard signs on your own lot.

faqs.q: What is a typical Troy home worth?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 median for owner-occupied homes is $420,300. Individual houses vary with age, lot and district.

faqs.q: When do Troy tax bills come due?
faqs.a: Summer bills are payable until September 1 and winter bills until February 14. Anything unpaid on March 1 goes to Oakland County.

faqs.q: Do Troy taxes reset after I sell?
faqs.a: For the buyer, yes. Taxable value uncaps in the calendar year after a transfer of ownership.

faqs.q: Which school district is a Troy house in?
faqs.a: Most houses are in Troy School District, but Avondale, Birmingham, Bloomfield Hills, Lamphere, Royal Oak and Warren Consolidated also cover parts of the city.

faqs.q: Where is a Troy deed recorded?
faqs.a: With the Oakland County Register of Deeds at 248-858-0597. Transfer tax is collected unless the deed cites an exemption.
